Both disclosures highlight the risk that product defects cause significant remediation expenses, reputation damage, and loss of market share. 2024 D004 cites 'Defects in our products have caused and could cause us to incur significant expenses to remediate and could damage our business.' 2025 D033 cites 'Defects in our products have caused and could cause us to incur significant expenses to remediate, which can damage our reputation and cause us to lose market share.'

materiality_analysis.reason: The disclosure expands the consequences of product defects to explicitly include 'reputation damage' and 'lose market share'. While the core risk (defects causing remediation costs) remains, the explicit quantification/consequence of market share loss and reputational harm represents a meaningful escalation in the disclosed risk exposure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Complex products may contain defects leading to loss of market acceptance, recall costs, and litigation, while AMD faces potential product liability claims for injuries that could have a material adverse effect if uninsured or exceeding coverage.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD identify product defects as a material risk involving significant remediation costs and potential damage to the business. NVDA highlights that defects cause 'significant expenses to remediate,' while AMD explicitly states that 'Costs related to defective products could have a material adverse effect on us.' Both companies acknowledge the complexity of their products increases the likelihood of defects; AMD notes that products 'may contain defects or failures when first introduced' and that testing cannot assure errors will not be found, whereas NVDA generally states defects 'have caused and could cause' these issues. Additionally, both disclose risks related to litigation and reputation, with AMD specifically mentioning 'defending against litigation... and damage to our reputation' and NVDA noting the risk to 'damage our business."

sentences.text: • Defects in our products have caused and could cause us to incur significant expenses to remediate and could damage our business.
Costs related to defective products could have a material adverse effect on us.

We cannot assure you that, despite our testing procedures, errors will not be found in new products or releases after commencement of commercial shipments in the future, which could result in loss of or delay in market acceptance of our products, material recall and replacement costs, loss of revenue, writing down the inventory of defective products, the diversion of the attention of our engineering personnel from product development efforts, defending against litigation related to defective products or related liabilities, including property damage, personal injury, damage to our reputation in the industry and loss of data or intangible property, and could adversely affect our relationships with our customers.
